card.name: Ganggangsullae
card.tagline: Korean women's moonlit harvest circle dance
card.profile: Ganggangsullae is a seasonal harvest and fertility ritual of southwestern Korea, performed primarily at Chuseok (Korean Thanksgiving) in the eighth lunar month (UNESCO). Under the full moon, women join hands in a circle and sing and dance all night under a lead singer, with the group answering the refrain 'ganggangsullae'; during interludes they mime farm and fishing-village vignettes. Traditionally performed only by women at night without instruments, it offered a rare freedom from restrictive Joseon-era rules governing rural young women.
card.insight: Designated an Important Intangible Cultural Property of Korea in 1966 and inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List in 2009, ganggangsullae is now taught in elementary-school music curricula and performed nationwide as a representative Korean folk art (UNESCO; Korea Heritage Service).
